# 1 Chronicles Chapter 20 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 380v–381r

---

**20:1** And-it-was at-the-time of-the-return of-the-year [litshuvat ha-shanah], at-the-time of-the-going-out of-the-kings [tset ha-melakhim], and-led Yo'av the-force of-the-army, and-destroyed [vayyashchet] the-land of-the-sons of-Ammon, and-came and-besieged [vayyatsar] Rabbah. And-David [was] sitting [yoshev] in-Yerushalayim. And-struck Yo'av Rabbah and-destroyed-it [vayyeherseha].

**20:2** And-took David the-crown of-their-king [malkam] from-upon his-head, and-found-it [to be] a-weight [mishqal] of-a-talent [kikkar] of-gold, and-in-it [was] a-precious stone [even yeqarah], and-it-was on the-head of-David. And-the-plunder [shelal] of-the-city he-brought-out, very much.

**20:3** And-the-people who [were] in-it he-brought-out, and-he-set [vayyasar] [them to work] with-the-saw [ba-meggerah] and-with-the-iron-picks [ba-charitsey ha-barzel] and-with-the-axes [uva-megzerot]. And-thus David did to-all the-cities of-the-sons of-Ammon. And-returned David and-all the-people to-Yerushalayim.

**20:4** And-it-was after this, and-stood [vatta'amod] battle [milchamah] in-Gezer with the-Pelishtim. Then struck Sibbkhai the-Chushati Sippai, from-the-offspring [miyildey] of-the-Refa'im, and-they-were-subdued [vayyikkane'u].

**20:5** And-there-was again battle with the-Pelishtim, and-struck Elchanan son of-Ya'ir Lachmi, the-brother of-Golyat [Goliath] the-Gitti, and-the-shaft [ets] of-his-spear [chanito] [was] like-a-weaver's beam [menor oregim].

**20:6** And-there-was again battle in-Gat, and-there-was a-man of-stature [middah], and-his-fingers [etsbe'otav] and-his-toes [were] six and-six, twenty-four, and-also he was-born to-the-Rapha [ha-rafa].

**20:7** And-he-taunted [vayecharef] Yisra'el, and-struck-him Yehonatan son of-Shim'a, brother of-David.

**20:8** These were-born to-the-Rapha in-Gat, and-they-fell by-the-hand of-David and-by-the-hand of-his-servants.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — The Great Omission:** The most theologically significant silence in all of Chronicles occurs between 20:1a and 20:1b. The phrase "And David was sitting in Jerusalem" is the same sentence that in 2 Samuel 11:1 launches the Bathsheba narrative — David's adultery, the murder of Uriah, Nathan's rebuke, the death of the child (2 Sam 11-12). The Chronicler deletes the entire sequence. Where Samuel devotes two full chapters to David's greatest sin, Chronicles offers a seamless transition from siege to victory. This is not accidental — it is deliberate theological editing. The Chronicler presents David as the ideal temple-preparer; the Bathsheba affair would compromise that portrait.

**v.2 — "their king" / "Milcom":** The Hebrew *malkam* can be read as "their king" or as "Milcom" (the Ammonite deity). If the latter, David seizes the crown from the idol's head — a theological triumph. The ambiguity is preserved in the consonantal text.

**v.3 — Forced labor or execution?:** The Hebrew *vayyasar* is debated. It may mean "he set them to work with saws" (forced labor) or "he sawed them" (execution). 2 Samuel 12:31 is equally ambiguous. Most modern translations favor forced labor; the Chronicler likely intends the same as his source.

**v.5 — "Lahmi, the brother of Goliath":** In 2 Samuel 21:19, "Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite killed Goliath the Gittite." The Chronicler resolves the apparent contradiction with 1 Samuel 17 (David kills Goliath) by specifying that Elhanan killed *Lahmi, brother of Goliath*. The name "Lahmi" may be extracted from "Bethlehemite" (*beit ha-lachmi*). This is a classic harmonizing revision.

*— EMET*
